headline: November scrap settles $20-30 a ton higher; Chicago shred up $30
detail: Mills paid about $30 a gross ton more for shred and heavy melt and $20 more for busheling in November, with Chicago mills chasing heavy grades that have been short since summer. Higher mill bids should keep yard prices for steel scrap firm into December.

headline: Copper bounces Monday after its worst week since March
detail: COMEX copper rose about 1.9% to roughly $6.36 a pound as Chinese buyers scrambled for metal and Shanghai premiums hit records. Big COMEX stocks may limit how much of that squeeze reaches US scrap prices.

headline: Fed's Waller backs a December rate hike and is open to a half point
detail: Waller said inflation is still too high and he leans toward a hike even if today's CPI improves. More hikes tend to lift the dollar, which weighs on metal prices.

headline: China's October exports rose 35% and imports 42%
detail: China's trade surplus passed $1 trillion for the year, and imports jumped. Strong imports point to healthy appetite for raw materials like copper ahead of a Trump-Xi meeting next week.

headline: Copper edges up again Tuesday as China's import premium hits a record
detail: LME copper was up about 0.3% early Tuesday, and the premium Chinese buyers pay for imported copper reached a record $230 a ton. Tight nearby supply supports copper and copper scrap prices.

headline: BC unions refuse to handle copper from the striking Highland Valley mine
detail: The BC Federation of Labour asked about 500,000 workers not to move or process output from Teck's Highland Valley mine, where 1,200 workers are on strike. Less concentrate reaching smelters tightens copper supply.

headline: Nucor lifts its hot-rolled coil price $15 to $1,295 a ton
detail: Nucor raised its weekly spot price again on Monday after pausing extra sales last week. Rising steel prices help mills keep paying up for scrap.

headline: Gold and silver ease ahead of this morning's inflation report
detail: Gold slipped to about $4,115 and silver near $53 on profit-taking after Monday's gains, with markets pricing a high chance of a December Fed hike. A hot CPI number could push them lower.

headline: Platinum climbs to a near three-week high
detail: Platinum rose above $1,570 an ounce Monday, up from a one-year low near $1,430 last week. Analysts still expect a surplus this year, which caps catalytic converter values.

headline: Cleveland-Cliffs reaches new four-year deals with the steelworkers union
detail: Tentative contracts cover about 12,000 workers at plants and mines in Indiana, Ohio and other states. That removes a strike risk at one of the Midwest's biggest steel and scrap buyers.

headline: China's October steel exports and iron ore imports both fall
detail: Chinese steel exports dropped about 6% from September and iron ore imports fell about 4%. Softer Chinese steel activity weighs on iron ore and world steel prices.

headline: China's factory-gate prices rise 5.7%, the fastest in over four years
detail: October producer prices beat forecasts, driven by energy and coal costs. Higher Chinese costs make its metal exports less cheap on world markets.

headline: China extends its tariff truce with the US for two more months
detail: Beijing keeps its extra 24% tariff on US goods suspended, leaving only 10%, ahead of a Trump-Xi meeting at APEC. Calmer trade ties help metals demand sentiment.

headline: Copper had its worst week since March as AI stocks fell and tariff odds faded
detail: LME copper fell about 2.6% last week to its lowest since July. The midterm results cut the chance of US copper tariffs, and the COMEX premium over London briefly turned to a discount, which squeezes US scrap spreads.

headline: Molson Coors takes a $30 million hit from the high Midwest aluminum premium
detail: The brewer blamed the US delivered aluminum premium for big cost increases and cut its outlook. A high premium supports prices paid for domestic aluminum scrap like cans.

headline: Nickel jumps to a five-week high on an Indonesian mining crackdown
detail: LME nickel rose about 4% after Indonesia moved against companies tied to a big ore trader. Tighter nickel supply supports stainless steel scrap values.

headline: Canada extends its tariff relief program but drops aluminum wire and extrusions
detail: Ottawa extended exemptions from its retaliatory tariffs to mid-2028, but aluminum wire and extrusions come off the list in February. Canada keeps its tariffs on US steel and aluminum.

headline: Stellantis keeps its Windsor assembly plant idle for a fourth week
detail: The plant stays down this week and a Nov 16 restart isn't confirmed, with the company citing demand and tariffs. Less auto production means less factory stamping scrap in the region.

headline: Honda plans a $3 billion assembly plant in Ohio
detail: The new plant near Marysville is due to start in 2029 building 240,000 vehicles a year. It adds future Midwest steel demand and stamping scrap.

headline: Plans for new commercial buildings dropped 9% in October
detail: Dodge's measure of projects entering planning fell as data center and warehouse plans cooled. That points to softer future demand for structural steel and wire.

headline: Mortgage rates ease a bit after the midterms but builders stay gloomy
detail: The 30-year rate averaged about 7.18%, down from a mid-October peak, but builder confidence is the lowest since 2012. Weak housing means soft demand for copper, wire and rebar.

headline: Chicago Fed's Goolsbee warns the AI building boom looks like overheating
detail: Goolsbee said the Fed must fix its inflation problem, pointing to rising service prices and data center spending. Another hawkish signal ahead of the December meeting supports the dollar.

headline: Gold bounced back above $4,100 Monday as the dollar softened
detail: Gold rose more than 1% as a weaker dollar offset Friday's strong jobs report. Silver gained even more, up nearly 3% on the day.

headline: Sibanye's US recycling profits jump while a Montana strike cuts palladium output
detail: Sibanye-Stillwater's US recycling arm earned 54% more on higher metal prices, but a strike cut its Montana mine output forecast. Less mined palladium is mildly supportive for converter values.

headline: Codelco admits it overstated copper output by 42,100 tons
detail: Chile's state miner booked unfinished material as finished copper and expects this year's output near 1.2 million tons. It underlines how tight mine supply is.

headline: Falling acid prices squeeze Chinese copper smelters toward output cuts
detail: Smelters are losing money on processing fees and sulfuric acid sales, and managers expect cuts. Less refined copper from China would lift demand for copper scrap as feed.

headline: October US new-vehicle sales pace slips below 16 million
detail: About 1.3 million vehicles sold, a 15.6 million yearly pace and the first reading under 16 million since February. Slower sales can mean slower production and less auto scrap.

headline: LME aluminum stocks keep falling
detail: London aluminum stocks fell to about 228,750 tons and cancelled warrants jumped. Shrinking stocks keep aluminum prices and scrap values high.

headline: Canada says tougher trade talks with the US have started
detail: Prime Minister Carney said Canada has dropped some red lines and Trump says a deal is coming soon. A deal could eventually ease US tariffs on Canadian steel and aluminum.

headline: Construction spending fell 1.9% in September, led by housing
detail: Home building spending dropped 5.5% while nonresidential rose 1.1%. Weak housing softens demand for rebar, wire and copper.
